- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.16) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If recent history shows a sharp spike followed by a drop, model tends to overshoot downward — cap forecast decline at 10% below peak.  
- When sentiment is positive (especially > 0.27) and forecast is falling, avoid undercorrecting — raise forecast by 0.5–1.5% to capture sentiment-driven rebound.  
- Model often overestimates mean reversion in short-term (1–3 days) — apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.  
- If forecast is > 10% above recent 7-day average and sentiment is negative, reduce forecast by 2–3% to avoid “sentiment mismatch” overcorrection.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently 3–5% below forecast, apply a 1–2% downward adjustment to future forecasts unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
